exposure: Discrepancies between prenatal expectations (towards partner and child) and postpartum reality
cohort: The study included 117 mothers of infants up to 12 months of age.
finding: Prenatal expectations, perceived stress levels, and maternal sense of competence were identified as significant factors in bonding difficulties, with postpartum depression symptoms also playing an important role as a single variable.
cross-section timing: Mothers of infants up to 12 months of age
